primary_claim: gpt-oss-20b shows robust resistance to jailbreaking via system-prompt attacks (100% refusal) and refusal-direction ablation across all 24 layers (100% refusal), though supervised fine-tuning on an uncensored teacher model's outputs partially succeeds at eliciting harmful outputs.

effect.value: system prompting: 100% refusal (0/100 broken, 3 prompts tried); refusal-direction ablation: 100% refusal across all 24 layers (10 samples/layer); SFT: partial success (50 samples)

contradicts_or_qualifies: Arditi et al.'s 'Refusal in LLMs is mediated by a single direction' finding — ablating the refusal direction did not successfully bypass refusal for gpt-oss-20b in this replication
stated_future_work: Try more automated red teaming/interp techniques.
limitations_stated: Not sure if JailbreakBench and HarmBench overlap and the fine-tuned model is just memorizing/overfitting rather than genuinely uncensored.
vllm mysteriously breaks after 60-80 samples, limiting sample sizes.
gpt-oss is still tricky to work with and not all libraries support its idiosyncrasies (Mxfp4, openai harmony chat format).
Research results can be difficult to extend to new models.
quote: Gpt oss seems to have robust safety training to both system prompting and refusal vector attacks.
